title: Potato Gratin
description:
Nothing’s quite like a hot and cheesy potatoes, such as twice-baked potatoes, or the bacon-potato cake, or this – a simple gratin.
In this recipe, from Fine Cooking, a number of alternatives are offered, from relatively simple to a bit more complicated. But the idea is straight- forward, put in what you’re in the mood for, or what you have in the house, or what you have time to prepare. Then, just enjoy this luscious treat.
They recommend reading the recipe through (always good advice) and making your plans before you start, choosing the essential ingredients and then the optional ones. We made this the other day with prosciutto, parsley, and a cheddar-jack cheese because that was what we had around and like.
START TO FINISH: 45 MINUTES
Potato Gratin
Layer on any combination of optional ingredients.
Top with the remaining potatoes, spreading them evenly, and pour over any liquid remaining in the pan.
Evenly scatter your choice of toppings over the potatoes.
Bake the gratin until it’s bubbly, the top is brown, and the potatoes are completely tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Let the gratin sit for about 10 minutes or longer so the liquid is fully absorbed and the layers are cohesive.
ingredients: 2-2½ pounds potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
2½ cups cream (heavy or light), half-and half, whole or low-fat milk, chicken broth, or some combination of above
Sharp Cheddar, or breadcrumbs with butter drizzled on
directions: Simmer the potatoes in your liquid in a big pot with a generous grinding of salt and a little pepper for 8 to 10 minutes, until just tender (almost al dente).
Choose you own special combination of optional ingredients.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer half the potatoes to the gratin dish and spread them evenly.
